entries.title: OR-License: Evaluating LLM Agents as Real-World Operations Research Practitioners
entries.summary: Can large language model (LLM) agents deliver expert-level operations research (OR) solutions directly from original client materials, without prior expert reformulation?
entries.why: Evaluates large language model agents as real-world operations research practitioners from client materials.

entries.title: OpenVLHarness: Real World Visual Agentic Tool-Use with Multimodal Memory
entries.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have made rapid progress on visual reasoning, yet many tasks require evidence that is difficult to obtain through internal reasoning alone: our controlled study on 22 benchmarks shows that simply increasing the inference budget of the…
entries.why: Studies real-world visual agentic tool-use with multimodal memory across multiple benchmarks.

entries.title: Introducing Timestral
entries.summary: State-of-the-art probabilistic forecasting in four sizes (5M–209M params), CPU-efficient, zero-shot ready.
entries.why: Provides CPU-efficient, zero-shot ready probabilistic forecasting in four distinct sizes.

entries.title: Self-Evolving Coding Agents via Harness-Policy Optimization
entries.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents have shown promising potential in coding tasks, and their performance is jointly determined by the policy model and the harness that mediates their interaction with the environment.
entries.why: Examines self-evolving coding agents through joint policy and harness optimization.

entries.title: AnyGoal: On World Model Generalization Beyond Expert Rollouts
entries.summary: The goal of a world model is to capture the dynamics of an environment. This has the great appeal that it allows agents to plan and simulate a course of actions with the help of a world model.
entries.why: Explores world model generalization beyond expert rollouts for planning and simulation.

entries.title: BlenderWorld: Benchmarking Visual Agents for 3D Creation from Real-World References
entries.summary: Recent advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have enabled them to act as autonomous agents, creating and editing 3D models via code or direct software manipulation.
entries.why: Benchmarks visual agents for creating and editing 3D models from real-world references.

entries.title: How Claude designed protein binders against scorpion neurotoxins
entries.summary: We asked an internal research Claude model to design minibinders (small proteins that attach tightly to a target) against scorpion neurotoxins.
entries.why: Demonstrates how an internal research model designed minibinders against scorpion neurotoxins.

entries.title: ALTK-Evolve: How learned memory tops the τ²-bench leaderboard on customer service tasks without a frontier model
entries.why: Shows how learned memory tops customer service benchmarks without a frontier model.

entries.title: How To Use Decision Models for Evals
entries.summary: Decision models have exploded onto the scene recently, starting with TypeSafe’s Jev, followed by Perplexity’s Decider, Liquid’s d1, Cloudflare’s Clef, and OpenAI’s Decisions API1. These models promise fast, inexpensive classification.
entries.why: Analyzes the recent explosion of decision models for fast, inexpensive classification.
